hints: For every part, split the boat’s velocity into a part across the river and a part along it. The across part alone sets the crossing time; the along part (plus the river) sets the drift.
worded:
1. Data: boat 5 m/s in still water, river 3 m/s, width 500 m. Crossing time = width ÷ (across component); drift = (along component) × time.

2. i.  Least time: point straight across, so all 5 m/s is across: 500/5 = 100 s. The river carries the boat 3 × 100 = 300 m downstream.

3. ii. Cross and come back to the start: each crossing must have zero net drift, so head upstream with 3 m/s of the 5 cancelling the river, leaving 4 m/s across: 2 × 500/4 = 250 s. (A numerical check confirms that no pair of unequal headings does better.)

4. iii. 500 m along the river and back: 500/(5 + 3) + 500/(5 − 3) = 62.5 + 250 = 312.5 s.

5. iv. To reach the point opposite: sin θ = 3/5 upstream of the normal, θ = 37°, i.e. 90° + 37° = 127° with the direction of flow.

6. v.  Heading at 120° to the flow: the across component is 5 sin 120° = 2.5√3 m/s, so t = 500/(2.5√3) = 200/√3 ≈ 115 s.
conventional:
![](asset:P000271-sol-1)

Let $v_{b} = 5$ m/s, $v_{r} = 3$ m/s, $W = 500$ m.

(i) $t_{\min} = \frac{W}{v_{b}} = 100$ s; drift $= v_{r}t_{\min} = 300$ m.

(ii) $t = \frac{2W}{\sqrt{v_{b}^{2} - v_{r}^{2}}} = \frac{1000}{4} = 250$ s.

(iii) $t = \frac{500}{5 + 3} + \frac{500}{5 - 3} = 62.5 + 250 = 312.5$ s.

(iv) $\sin\theta = \frac{v_{r}}{v_{b}} = \frac{3}{5} \Rightarrow \theta = 37^{\circ}$ upstream of the normal, i.e. $127^{\circ}$ with the flow.

(v) $t = \frac{W}{v_{b}\sin 120^{\circ}} = \frac{500}{5\left( \sqrt{3}/2 \right)} = \frac{200}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 115$ s.
mistakes: In (iii), going downstream and back takes longer than 2 × 500/5 = 200 s: the slow leg dominates.
In (iv) and (v), angles “with the flow” are measured from the downstream direction; 127° and 120° both point partly upstream.

check.solved_answer: (i) 100 s, 300 m; (ii) 250 s; (iii) 312.5 s; (iv) 127° with the direction of flow (37° upstream of the normal); (v) $200/\sqrt{3}$ s ≈ 115 s.
